profiles.Summary: Batman: Arkham Knight is a demanding open-world action game that runs playably on the Steam Deck, sitting comfortably above the minimum PC GPU spec (GTX 660) but below the recommended (GTX 760). With FSR upscaling and medium-to-low settings it can hold a stable 30–40 fps, making it a solid Deck experience despite its heavy rain and particle effects.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck–specific reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On your first run, check frame rate during a Batmobile chase in open Gotham — that is the heaviest workload — and drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if it stutters below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal; the 30 Hz refresh lock eliminates tearing and reduces APU power draw. Disabling all post-process effects (film grain, chromatic aberration, rain drops) yields the biggest battery gains in this title.

KnownIssues: The PC version had a notoriously troubled launch with widespread performance issues; some residual stuttering in open-world Gotham sections may still occur.
Rain, particle effects, and Batmobile combat sequences are significantly more GPU-intensive than on-foot gameplay and can cause frame dips.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 1280x800 at high settings pushes the Deck hard; expect 60 fps only in quieter indoor areas and plan for 40-50 fps in open Gotham with rain. Consider capping at 40 fps via Quick Access if you see frequent dips, and keep a charger nearby.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives perfectly smooth pacing that suits Arkham Knight's cinematic style; FSR at 1024x640 recovers sharpness while keeping GPU headroom for open-world streaming. Shadow Quality is the primary lever — drop it to Low if the Batmobile sections cause dips.
